newsitem.title: USA: Conflicting reports circulate about Sinatra health.
newsitem.headline: Conflicting reports circulate about Sinatra health.

text.p: Legendary entertainer Frank Sinatra remained in a hospital on Friday amid reports that his health problems have become more serious than announced.

When Sinatra entered Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre a week ago, the 80-year-old singer's publicist and a hospital spokesman said it was only for treatment of a "pinched nerve." But that has been followed by an unexplained extension of his hospital stay and conflicting reports about his condition.
Army Archerd, a leading Hollywood columnist who writes for Daily Variety, said on Tuesday that Sinatra's daughter, Nancy Sinatra, told him her father had a slight case of pneumonia.

Los Angeles TV station KCBS, citing an unnamed source, said on Friday that Sinatra's condition had worsened and he was being treated for "heart failure" as well as pneumonia. It said Sinatra's hospital room at Cedars-Sinai resembled an intensive care unit but that he wanted to go home against his doctor's orders.

Giving a different picture, the Cable News Network said on Friday that talk show host Larry King had spoken with someone close to Sinatra who said the singer was not in "serious danger." Sinatra was said to be in guarded condition while recovering from pneumonia and doctors were "keeping a very close eye on him," according to CNN.

Sinatra's publicist, Susan Reynolds, earlier denied reports that he was seriously ill when he entered the hospital on Nov. 1. She refused to answer questions about his health Friday, saying "Mr. Sinatra has reconfirmed his request that there be no comment on his condition until he is released from the hospital." Hospital officials have also remained silent.

Sinatra was originally expected to go home last weekend but doctors extended his hospital stay without explanation. In Tuesday's column, Archerd said Nancy Sinatra told him her father was feeling better after a minor bout of pneumonia.
Sinatra's other daughter, Tina, said the singer had been suffering from the pinched nerve "for several weeks" before being admitted to the hospital, Archerd wrote.
The hospital has received dozens of flower displays and hundreds of letters from Sinatra's fans and well-wishers.
